summary: The University of British Columbia's International Scholars Program offers need- and merit-based awards that can cover the full cost of a student's degree and living expenses — the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award is the best known.
covers: Need-based support up to the full cost of your programme and living expenses, renewable for up to three further years.

Four awards sit under the programme: the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award, the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award (for students from impoverished or war-torn areas), the International Impact Award (sustainability and climate leadership) and the Vantage One Excellence Award.
Separately, UBC automatically considers international applicants for merit entrance scholarships.
eligibility: International students who will study in Canada on a study permit, entering UBC directly from secondary school.
Superior academic achievement (all As or the equivalent) and significant financial need.
A nominator at your school (such as a counsellor or principal) and one teacher referee.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to UBC (the 2027-entry application is due in early October 2026 for scholarship candidates).
Submit the International Scholars Program application by 15 November 2026, with your nominator and referee details.
Upload transcripts and official test results by 31 January 2027.
Decisions are released between February and April 2027.
watch_out: The scholarship route needs an earlier admission application than UBC's usual deadline — check the exact date for 2027 entry.
Awards are need-based: you will submit detailed family financial information.
Only students coming straight from secondary school qualify; transfer students do not.

costs: The award — need-based, up to the full cost of your programme and living expenses
documents: Your UBC admission application — it opens in early October 2026
The International Scholars application by 15 November 2026: four short essays (about 150–250 words each) and detailed family finances — annual income and expenses, wealth and assets
A nominator at your school (such as your counsellor or principal) and a separate teacher referee
Transcripts and English test results by 31 January 2027, meeting UBC's English Language Admission Standard

faq.q: How much financial need do I have to show?
faq.a: Enough that a UBC degree would be impossible without meaningful financial help. The awards are for students who could not otherwise attend.
All As, or the equivalent in your curriculum.
UBC releases award decisions on a rolling basis between February and April 2027.
